d4-1.title: Walkthrough 1: complete normal execution
d4-1.alt: CLI config, GCC build, DWARF, GDB stop loop, trace assembly, JSON export, parser load/index, deep validation and consumer summary form one continuous pipeline.
d4-1.caption: Solid arrows are observed/control/data handoffs. The parser starts only after the JSON document is written; it does not rerun the engine.

d4-2.title: Walkthrough 2: recursion and activations
d4-2.alt: GDB reports nested recurse frames. The engine assigns activation IDs, captures caller frames with a configured depth, and the parser exposes frame-scoped variables without merging recursive activations.
d4-2.caption: Same function name and same variable name do not merge distinct activations; observed caller activity is not inferred variable lifetime.

d4-3.title: Walkthrough 3: malloc to lifetime
d4-3.alt: Linked --wrap_malloc calls the real allocator, updates a PID-local table, appends a sequenced event row, Rust reads complete rows, HeapTimeline ingests a verified prefix and final assembly records a lifetime.
d4-3.caption: The C wrapper writes a file; Rust does not call the C allocator directly. An event is observed telemetry, not an exact instruction timestamp.

d4-4.title: Walkthrough 4: free, reuse and realloc
d4-4.alt: Free closes a lifetime; a later allocation at the same address receives a new ID; realloc can be in-place, moved, failed or terminal-free. TP8-F01 requires recorded corroboration for predecessor links.
d4-4.caption: Address equality never proves object identity. A forged old ID without compatible events becomes unavailable or contradictory.

d4-5.title: Walkthrough 5: pointer observation and provenance
d4-5.alt: GDB records a pointer variable and its numeric target. Heap containment yields an address candidate; provenance status and recorded identity decide whether any allocation relationship is definite.
d4-5.caption: A pointer value is observed. An address match is not allocation origin; ambiguous reuse remains ambiguous.

d4-6.title: Walkthrough 6: DWARF type information
d4-6.alt: GCC emits DWARF; the extractor indexes CU/DIE type and declaration records; runtime variables reference trace-local IDs; the parser exposes type/declaration metadata without decoding Stage 2 typed memory.
d4-6.caption: DWARF supplies static type/declaration metadata. It does not prove that a member was initialized or that a source expression executed.

d4-7.title: Walkthrough 7: Clang AST and fusion
d4-7.alt: Optional Clang extracts declarations and source spans. Fusion correlates DWARF and AST declarations and forms heap-call source candidates; ambiguity is explicit and never proves execution.
d4-7.caption: Static source metadata and runtime observations remain separate. A same-line call is a candidate, not a dynamic call proof.

d4-8.title: Walkthrough 8: crash and partial evidence
d4-8.alt: GDB observes a fatal signal; the engine captures a partial snapshot and crash report, optional diagnostics remain separate, and the parser preserves partial coverage without inventing observations.
d4-8.caption: A crash is a recorded execution outcome. Missing observations stay missing; tool reports do not become primary-run identities.

d4-9.title: Walkthrough 9: infinite loop and limits
d4-9.alt: A bounded loop reaches a step or wall limit. The engine retains attempted positions, events, snapshots and gaps, then exports a partial trace; the parser distinguishes attempts from retained events.
d4-9.caption: A step limit is not a proof of nontermination. Attempted instruction counts and retained event counts are different.

d4-10.title: Walkthrough 10: fork and heap coverage
d4-10.alt: Fork resets child allocator state; parent and logged child append PID-local events and ACKs. The parser verifies observed PIDs and followed inferior, while silent descendants remain unknown.
d4-10.caption: Complete observed-PID history is not a descendant census. Missing ACKs or silent children are not reconstructed.

d4-11.title: Walkthrough 11: parser from the inside
d4-11.alt: JSON loading builds a canonical Arc store and position indexes. Borrowed views resolve evidence, deep validation creates a report, TP-6 qualifies relationships and TP-7 composes bounded pages.
d4-11.caption: Loading is not validation. Queries borrow original records and never clone the canonical trace.

d4-12.title: Walkthrough 12: corrupted imported evidence
d4-12.alt: Schema-compatible mutations can forge pointer identity, process completeness or realloc predecessors. Deep validation emits structural findings and TP-6 downgrades confidence; raw records remain available.
d4-12.caption: Deserialization success is not evidence trustworthiness. Contradictory relationships are never promoted to definite.
